6-0-0.prompt: Rina was writing notes. A bell rang and interrupted her. Which description is most accurate?
6-0-0.answer: Rina was writing when the bell rang.
options: Rina was writing when the bell rang.
Rina wrote when the bell was ringing every day.
Rina is writing when the bell rang.
Rina had writing when the bell ring.
6-0-0.hint: Use past continuous for the background action and past simple for the interruption.

6-0-1.prompt: Two actions happened: the pupils were revising at 8 pm; the lights suddenly went out. Choose the correct report.
6-0-1.answer: The pupils were revising when the lights went out.
options: The pupils were revising when the lights went out.
The pupils revised when the lights were go out.
The pupils are revising when the lights went out.
The pupils have revising when lights went out.
6-0-1.hint: Background action takes were + -ing; the interruption uses past simple.

6-0-2.prompt: Which sentence shows that one past activity was interrupted by another?
6-0-2.answer: She was crossing the road when a car stopped.
options: She was crossing the road when a car stopped.
She crossing the road when a car stop.
She crosses the road when a car stops daily.
She had crossed while a car will stop.
6-0-2.hint: Was crossing describes an ongoing past activity.

6-1-0.prompt: Farid started training in January and is still training in October. Choose the correct sentence.
options: Farid has trained since January.
Farid trained since January yesterday.
Farid is trained for January.
Farid will train since January.
6-1-0.hint: Since gives the starting point of an action continuing to now.

6-1-1.prompt: A family moved to Muar five years ago and still lives there. Which is correct?
6-1-1.answer: They have lived in Muar for five years.
options: They have lived in Muar for five years.
They lived in Muar since five years.
They are lived at Muar for five years.
They will lived in Muar for years.
6-1-1.hint: Use present perfect with for + duration.

6-1-2.prompt: Your friend asks about lifetime experience rather than yesterday. Choose the best question.
options: Have you ever visited Langkawi?
Did you ever visited Langkawi yesterday?
Have you visit Langkawi last Tuesday?
Do you visited Langkawi last month?
6-1-2.hint: Have you ever + past participle asks about life experience.

6-2-0.prompt: A school trip depends on the weather tomorrow. Choose a realistic first conditional.
6-2-0.answer: If it rains tomorrow, we will visit the museum instead.
options: If it rains tomorrow, we will visit the museum instead.
If it will rain tomorrow, we visit the museum yesterday.
If it rained tomorrow, we will visited the museum.
If it rains tomorrow, we visited yesterday.
6-2-0.hint: First conditional uses if + present and will + base verb.

6-2-1.prompt: A student wants to improve her marks. Which first conditional gives sensible advice?
6-2-1.answer: If she practises daily, she will improve.
options: If she practises daily, she will improve.
If she will practises daily, she improves yesterday.
If she practised daily, she will improved.
If she practices daily, she was improving last week.
6-2-1.hint: Combine present simple condition with will + verb.

6-2-2.prompt: Choose the conditional that correctly links a possible event with its result.
6-2-2.answer: If the bus arrives on time, we will reach school early.
options: If the bus arrives on time, we will reach school early.
If the bus will arrive on time, we reached school yesterday.
If the bus arriving on time, we will reached school.
If the bus arrived on time, we arrives school.
6-2-2.hint: Possible future: if + present, will + verb.

6-3-0.prompt: A newspaper reports that volunteers collected rubbish yesterday. Which passive version is correct?
6-3-0.answer: The rubbish was collected by volunteers yesterday.
options: The rubbish was collected by volunteers yesterday.
The rubbish is collect by volunteers yesterday.
The rubbish collected by volunteers was yesterday.
The rubbish were collecting volunteers yesterday.

6-3-1.prompt: A recipe explains that fresh bread is prepared every morning. Which passive sentence fits?
6-3-1.answer: Fresh bread is made every morning.
options: Fresh bread is made every morning.
Fresh bread are making every morning.
Fresh bread were made every mornings.
Fresh bread is make every morning.
6-3-1.hint: Uncountable bread is followed by is made.

6-3-2.prompt: The principal announced that the medals were presented to winners. Which sentence is correctly passive?
6-3-2.answer: The medals were presented to the winners.
options: The medals were presented to the winners.
The medals was presenting to the winners.
The medals were present the winners.
The medals presented by the winners yesterday are.
6-3-2.hint: Plural medals takes were + past participle.

6-4-0.prompt: Lina said, "I am preparing for the competition." Report this later.
6-4-0.answer: Lina said that she was preparing for the competition.
options: Lina said that she was preparing for the competition.
Lina said that I am preparing for the competition.
Lina said that she is prepare for competition.
Lina said she were prepared the competition.
6-4-0.hint: Backshift am preparing to was preparing and change I to she.

6-4-1.prompt: A boy said, "I will help you." Which sentence reports this correctly?
6-4-1.answer: He said that he would help me.
options: He said that he would help me.
He said he will helped me.
He said I would helping him.
He said he would helped him.
6-4-1.hint: Will usually changes to would, followed by base verb.

6-5-0.prompt: You see dark clouds, but the forecast is uncertain. Which statement shows possibility?
options: It might rain this afternoon.
It must rain this afternoon for sure.
It cannot rain because of clouds.
It has rained yesterday tomorrow.

6-5-1.prompt: A sign says "No entry — laboratory." Which instruction is strongest and correct?
6-5-1.answer: You must not enter the laboratory.
options: You must not enter the laboratory.
You might enter the laboratory.
You should enter without permission.
You can enter whenever you like.

6-6-0.prompt: A traveller says, "I arrived in 2021 and still work here." Which reply is accurate?
options: You have worked here since 2021.
You worked here for 2021 every day.
You were working here since 2021 tomorrow.
You work since four years ago.
6-6-0.hint: Since identifies a start point for present perfect.

6-6-1.prompt: At 6 pm yesterday, Sam was practising. Then the power failed. Which account fits?
6-6-1.answer: Sam was practising when the power failed.
options: Sam was practising when the power failed.
Sam practises when the power was fail.
Sam has practising when the power failed.
Sam practising when power has failing.
6-6-1.hint: Continuous action was interrupted in the past.

6-7-0.prompt: Road repairs are almost complete. Choose the grammatically correct prediction.
6-7-0.answer: If workers finish today, the road will open tomorrow.
options: If workers finish today, the road will open tomorrow.
If workers will finish today, the road opened yesterday.
If workers finished today, the road will opened tomorrow.
If workers finishes today, the road are opening yesterday.

6-7-1.prompt: The school rules require helmets for cycling. Choose a correct statement.
6-7-1.answer: Helmets must be worn when cycling.
options: Helmets must be worn when cycling.
Helmets must wearing when cycling.
Helmets might be wore by students yesterday.
Helmets must be wear when cycling.
6-7-1.hint: Modal passive uses must be + past participle.
